subject: Re: ClarityHealth — migration economics & price-match proposal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: JP Patterson <jpatterson@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: ClarityHealth — migration economics & price-match proposal

Hi JP — great to meet yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled together an initial offer that addresses the two asks you raised: (1) price parity with your incumbent list rates, and (2) help offsetting migration / validation effort.

Summary (attached: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf):
- Hosted API: list rate parity for text generation calls (we will match the current per-token rates you shared)
- 12-month commitment term (option to convert to a 36-month reserved contract after pilot)
- One-time migration credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice (can be used for onboarding, benchmark lab time, or consumption)
- Technical SLA addendum and rollback triggers included in the redline (see redline_contract.docx)

Before I share this with procurement, two quick asks so I can firm numbers:
1) Confirm your 12-month forecasted monthly token volumes (a small sample CSV would help).
2) Are there any required egress/egress caps or data residency clauses beyond what we discussed?

If that aligns, I can route the redline through Legal + our Finance lead (Ben) and send a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf

From: JP Patterson <jpatterson@clarityhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clarityhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClarityHealth — migration economics & price-match proposal

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the quick turn. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

- The incumbent is charging us $0.0008 per token for generation. Can you confirm your matched rate includes the same token definition (generation vs. prompt tokens)? We need parity end-to-end, not just generation.
- The migration credit is helpful — procurement is pushing for a fixed onboarding discount instead of a credit bucket so it’s baked into TCV. Would Redwood consider converting the $50k credit into an equivalent 8% one-time onboarding discount against year-1 spend?
- We also need to see a draft SOW and a high-level runbook for rollback in case quality doesn't meet our benchmarks during pilot.

If you can get a redlined contract and the runbook over by EOD Wednesday, procurement will prioritize review.

Best,
JP Patterson
Head of Procurement
ClarityHealth

(Attachment stub: clarity_usage_snapshot.csv — 1.2MB, monthly token summary for past 6 months)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ClarityHealth — procurement asks (need quick decision)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding JP's reply and usage snapshot. Procurement wants token parity for both prompt+generation and prefers an onboarding discount folded into year-1 TCV rather than a siloed credit. They also want an SOW + rollback runbook.

My proposed counter (to avoid losing momentum):
- Convert $50k migration credit -> $40k upfront invoice credit + 4% additional year-1 discount (net effect ~ $50k for their forecast)
- Match per-token rates for prompt+generation (we should confirm the token definitions with Legal)
- Include a 30-day quality validation period: if fail, allow migration assistance refund (pro-rated) rather than a full rollback clause

Question for Ben: finance okay with $40k + 4%? It preserves some margin vs full $50k credit and gives procurement what they want (on-paper discount).

Marissa — recommend we hold to SLA language but be flexible on the mechanics of the credit. If you agree, I’ll send consolidated offer and ask for a redline on the SOW.

— Vivek

Vivek — quick thoughts:
- Ben: Converting to $40k + 4% sounds acceptable as a sales concession. Keep it time-limited to year-1 and make the 4% refundable only if quality gates fail during the 30-day validation window. Finance should retain final sign-off but this is within discretionary bounds.
- On token parity: insist on clear token definition in the MSA (prompt vs. generation) and cap any egress/transform fees — offer a 6-month egress grace for existing dataset transfers.
- Contract redline: attach our template with the SLA addendum and a short SOW placeholder. I’ll push Legal to pre-seed the redline so turnaround is <48 hours. (Attachment: redline_contract.docx)

Send the consolidated offer to JP as a single message with the redline and DocuSign link. Emphasize we can move quickly if they accept the terms.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

(Attachment stub: redline_contract.docx — 5 pages, SLA addendum and SOW placeholder)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: procurement@clarityhealth.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-01T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClarityHealth — migration economics & price-match proposal

JP — thanks for the clear asks. We discussed internally and can do the following consolidated offer: 

- Price parity: Redwood will match the incumbent per-token rate across both prompt and generation tokens at $0.0008/token for year-1 (detail in attached).
- Year-1 commercial mechanics: $40,000 onboarding credit applied to your first invoice + a 4% year-1 discount on billed consumption (equivalent to the migration assistance you requested).
- Validation & rollback: 30-day quality validation window post-go-live. If Redwood fails agreed-upon quality gates in that window, we will provide a pro-rated refund of the year-1 discount (details in redline_contract.docx).
- Egress: 6-month egress grace for dataset transfers (no charges).

Attachments: redline_contract.docx (redlined MSA + SLA addendum) and clarity_usage_snapshot.csv (your usage we referenced). If that sounds good I’ll route the redline through DocuSign and Legal — here’s a placeholder link: https://www.docusign.com/US/sign?e=example-doc-id

Would you like the SOW runbook to list specific acceptance tests or keep it at high level? We can mirror the standard Redwood validation checklist if that speeds review.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
